DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph 14 NOV 2019 OILG OPINION No. ATTY. MARIA SALVE-RUBAYA-ADAMOS OIC, Sanggunian Panlalawigan Secretary Sanggunian Panlalawigan ng Rizal Dear Atty. Adamos: s. 2012. This has reference your letter dated 19 July 2019 from Atty. Maria Salve- Rubaya-Adamos, OIC, Sangunian Panlalawigan Secretariat, requesting from DILG Region IV-A for opinion relative to the ordinance establishing a drug-free workplace and authorizing the drug testing for elective and appointive public officers and employees and for other purposes. Dangerous Drug Board issued Resolution No. 13, series of 2018 (DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018) on the Establishment and Institutionalization of Drug-free Workplace Policies in all Government Offices, including the Conduct of Authorized Drug Testing for Elective Local Officials and Appointive Public Officers and for Other Purposes. This resolution mandates all local sanggunians to enact their respective Ordinances on the establishment of drug free workplace policies within two (2) months from the effectivity of this Regulation. Accordingly, this Department issued Memorandum Circular No. 2018-013 (MC 2018-13) directing the regional and field officers to disseminate DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018 to ensure adoption and implementation of the same in their respective offices. Now, Sanggunian Panlalawigan ng Rizal issued Ordinance No. 07, series of 2019 (Ord. 7, s. 2019), which is an Ordinance Establishing and Institutionalizing Drug-Free Workplace Policies in all Government Offices in the Province of Rizal including the Conduct of Authorized Drug Testing for Elective Officials and Appointive Public Officers and Employees, and for Other Purposes. Atty. Adamos inquires, in verbatim, the following: I. Whether or not there is a need for the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal to approve a separate ordinance mandating all municipalities and city in its area of jurisdiction to enact their respective Drug-Free Workplace Ordinance; 2. Whether or not Civil Service Commission Memorandum Circular No. 13, s. 2017 (CSC MC 13, s. 2017) is superseded by DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018; 3. Whether or not Ord. 7, s. 2019 of the Sanggunian Panlalawigan ng Rizal is compliant to DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018.

On the first query, we lean toward the affirmative. Sections 468(a)(I)(5) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, states: Section 468. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (a) The sangguniang panlalawigan, as the legislative body of the province, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the genera/ welfare of the province and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the province as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: (2) Approve ordinances and pass resolutions necessary for an efficient and effective provincial government and, in this connection, shall: xxx (v) Enact ordinances intended to prevent, suppress and impose appropriate penalties for habitual drunkenness in public places, vagrancy, mendicancy, prostitution, establishment and maintenance of houses of ill repute, gambling and other prohibited games of chance, fraudulent devices and ways to obtain money or property, drug addiction, maintenance of drug dens, drug pushing, juvenile delinquency, the printing, distribution or exhibition of obscene or pornographic materials or publications, and other activities inimical to the welfare and morals of the inhabitants of the province; xxx Also, DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018 is presumed valid. This Department has no authority to rule on its validity or otherwise. Item No. IX(d) DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018 expressly states: IX. Responsibilities of Agencies Xxx d. All local Sanggunians shall enact their respective Ordinances mandating the establishment of drug free workplace policies within two (2) months from the effectivity of this Regulation. The Sanggunian Panlalawigan shall enact a Provincial Ordinance mandating the establishment of drug- free workplace policies in cities and municipalities under its jurisdiction. The Sanggunian Panlungsod and Sanggunian Bayan shall also enact their respective ordinances mandating the establishment of drug-free workplace policies in barangays. Failure to enact such Ordinance shall be cause for sanctions against responsible officials pursuant to Section 60

of the Local Government Code without prejudice to the filing ofa case for violation of Section 32, Article II, of the Act. On the second query, it is herein noted that CSC MC 13, s. 2017 provides for different scope/coverage and penalties than that of DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018. CSC MC 13, s. 2017 provides for interventions and rehabilitations whereas DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018 outrightly provides for administrative liabilities. Further, CSC MC 13, s. 2017 applies to all employees in the civil service with the express exclusion of contract of service and job order personnel whereas DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018 covers only appointive officials and elective officers with the inclusion of contract of service and job order personnel. Correspondingly, we shall defer to the comments, opinion, and/or recommendation of the CSC and DDB on the same. On the third query, we find that Ord. 7, s. 2019 is almost an exact reiteration of DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018. However, we noticed that the subject of Ord. 7, s. 2019 includes employees and that under Section II(f) of the same, it includes a penalty of dismissal from the service at the first offense whereas in DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018, it does not expressly include employees in the civil service and that it does not include a penalty of dismissal from service at the first offense. Thus, our view leans toward the negative i.e. the Ord. 7, s. 2019 is not fully compliant to DDB Reso. 13, s. 2018. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary MARIVEL SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary
